pr_title: Send enter/leave events for floating views
pr_body:
Previously we used a reparent event to detect when a view changes parent, then sent an output enter/leave to the surfaces if needed. This worked for tiling views but not floating views, as floating views can intersect another output without changing parent.

The solution implemented for floating views also applies cleanly to tiling views, so the previous method has been completely replaced and the reparent event has been removed.

This introduces a new function `container_discover_outputs`. This function compares the container's `current` position to the outputs, sends enter and leave events as needed, and keeps track of which outputs it's intersecting in a new `container->outputs` list. If it has entered a new output with a different scale then the title and marks textures will also be recreated at the new scale.

The function is called when a transaction applies. This is convenient as it means we don't have to call it from various places.

There is imperfect rendering when a floating view overlaps two outputs with different scales. It renders correctly for the most recently entered output, but there is only one title texture so it renders incorrectly on the old output.

To test:

* Move tiling containers to different outputs and check the title and marks textures scale
* Move floating containers so they overlap multiple outputs and see the new output renders the title and marks texture correctly
* Move a floating split container so it overlaps multiple outputs
* Hotplug outputs and make sure it doesn't crash - I haven't tested this

Debug log messages are printed when an enter or leave event occurs.

Fixes #2482 
Fixes #2485

issue_context.title: Workspaces from other outputs have incorrect scaling after unplugging
issue_context.body:
To test, have 2 outputs, one with a scale factor of 2 and one with a scale factor of 1.
Put some clients on workspaces on the second output (the one with scale = 1), then unplug the second output.
The workspaces then migrate to the first output (scale = 2) and clients are upscaled by the compositor, rather than letting them scale themselves. The only way to fix this is to move the clients to another non-empty workspace with correctly scaled clients.
I suppose the issue is that enter events are not sent when workspaces are migrated between outputs or between workspaces.

review_comments: Do we really need to maintain a list of entered outputs per non-view container?

Yes. If the container renders its own title (eg. a nested split) then the title texture needs to be recreated at the new scale when the container enters a new output.

Remember, the plan is for root, outputs and workspaces to not be part of `sway_container` any more, so the `outputs` property won't apply to them.
